7.C  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2024-001, a Resolution of the Planning Commission of the
  City of Palmdale, California, recommending City Council denial of General Plan
  Amendment 23-0001, Zone Change 23-0002, and Specific Plan Amendment 22-001; a
  request to amend the Antelope Valley Auto Center Specific Plan and change the
  General Plan Land Use Designation and Zone from Specific Plan to Regional
  Commercial, for approximately 20 acres located on the northwest and northeast corners
  of West Avenue Q and Carriage Way and find that the requests are exempt from
  Environmental Review (APNs: 3003 002 086, 099, -100, -103, -104, -105, And -106).

  Planning Manager Brenda Magaña presented this item.

  Chair Dean Henderson opened the Public Hearing.
 On behalf of Land Developers and Associates and the Applicant, Todd Bessire spoke in
support of the zone change, requesting the Commission consider changing the zone to
allow Regional Commercial.

Todd Bessire advised the Commission that the property has yet to be successful in
obtaining a user for a new dealership interested in purchasing the site for the use of a
dealership, mainly due to the economic shift of consumers using online options to make
buying vehicles. Additionally, this property has been marketed for the past seven years.
On behalf of the applicant, the request to change the zoning to allow Regional
Commercial use will allow for more viable use of the property.

Chair Dean Henderson asked if there is a project for this property.

Todd Bessire explained that the site cannot be marketed for the current use of an
automobile dealership. Future use and sale of the property will depend on the allowed
use, which will benefit the City.

Chair Dean Henderson asked who the owner is for the property.

Todd Bessire informed that Renaissance Holdings, LLC, and Land Developers and
Associates own seven acres, three parcels immediately south and adjacent to Auto
Center Drive, west of Carriage Way.

Chair Dean Henderson asked how long they have owned this site.

Todd Bessire advised that Land Developers and Associates have owned it for three
years, and Renaissance Holdings has owned it for seven years; the property has not
been successful in securing a buyer.

Commissioner Mateo Olivarez asked when the last time a dealership came to Palmdale.

Todd Bessire reported the last new dealership was developed over 30 years ago.

On behalf of Palmdale Roberston Honda, Bob Robertson introduced himself as the
owner for the past 30 years; he spoke in support of the zone change to allow for a wider
variety of potential users. Mr. Robertson informed Commissioners that he has sold the
business and maintains land ownership in the Palmdale Auto Mall. He enlisted the
services of a broker to assist in the sale of the property. However, there is little to no
interest once they become aware of the property’s allowable uses.

Commissioner David Lujan asked about Hertz’s recent announcement related to electric
vehicles.

Bob Robertson stated that the future of electric vehicles is the Hybrid model.

On behalf of Keller Williams, Broker Phil Terry spoke in support of the zone change. He
has directly marketed this site for potential dealerships for the last seven years, and has
been unsuccessful because of the restriction of uses with the Specific Plan.
   On behalf of Land Developers and Associates, Principal Daniel Singh spoke in support of
  the zone change.

  Chair Dean Henderson closed the Public Hearing.

RECOMMENDATION

The Planning Commission has the following options:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. PC-2023-026 approving Conditional Use Permit

  adopt the Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) and Mitigation Monitoring and

Option 1 is recommended.

BACKGROUND

On July 21, 2005, the Planning Commission approved Conditional Use Permit (CUP)
05-05, which was a request to construct an approximately 95,000 square foot pre-mixed
concrete packaging facility on a 20-acre site. On August 13, 2009, CUP 05-05 Major
Modification (MM) was approved to decrease the overall size of the facility from 95,000
square feet to approximately 80,000 square feet. The applicant was unable to inaugurate
the use during the initial approval period and the CUP expired. Subsequently, the
applicant submitted a new application (CUP 17-012) which was approved by the Planning
Commission on February 8, 2018, through Resolution No. PC-2018-006. Then, on June
10, 2021, the Planning Commission approved an application for a time extension (CUP
17-012 TE No. 1) of the previously approved project.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant is requesting approval of a Major Modification application to previously
approved CUP 17-012 Time Extension (TE) No. 1 and approval of SPR 22-019 to facilitate
the construction of the proposed project.

The Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) requires Major Modification and SPR application
approvals for the proposed project. The original project approval consists of two
contiguous parcels totaling approximately 20 acres, to be completed in three phases;
however, the proposed modification will increase the size of the development by
approximately 84,000 square feet.

Major Modification No. 1 includes the following:
   Expanding the entitled 20-acre project site by 10 acres (APN: 3024-002-007) for a
  total of three parcels totaling 30 acres;
   Construction of an additional 65,000 square feet for the purpose of a block paver
  manufacturing facility (Paveston);
   Reduction of the concrete packaging facility by 3,000 square feet;
   Addition of a 21,000-square-foot covered storage space to the facility;
   Reduction of the office building by 1,400 square feet; and,
   Reduction of the entire project into two phases instead of three.

Phase I will consist of constructing a 50,000-square-foot concrete packaging facility with
a 21,000-square-foot covered storage, a 3,600-square-foot office building, and two
detention basins. Phase 2 will consist of a 65,000-square-foot block paver manufacturing
facility and a 24,440-square-foot manufacturing facility.

The total building area for the proposed project is approximately 164,000 square feet. In
addition, the proposed project includes improvements such as curb, gutter, sidewalks,
parking, and landscaping needed to support the new development, including street
improvements across the project frontage, and approximately nine acres of outdoor
storage areas within the site. The project site contains western Joshua trees which will
be removed through an Incidental Take Permit (ITP) in accordance with the California
Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW).

Access

Street improvements will be constructed along the project frontage of East Palmdale
Boulevard which include two new driveways to access the site. Internal circulation will be
provided through a vehicular path around the manufacturing facility. The City Engineer
and Los Angeles County Fire Department have reviewed the project and determined that
it is designed with adequate access to accommodate safe vehicular flow. Furthermore,
access to the site will not be affected by the phasing of the development.

Architecture

The proposed materials and colors demonstrate earth tones. The proposed production
buildings will consist of rib metal roof and wall panels, fixed louvers, metal fascia, fixed
glass in aluminum frame, an accent band and decorative translucent panels. The
proposed office building will consist of a panel rib metal roof, metal fascia, exterior plaster,
and aluminum shade.

Use

The operational activities of the Quikrete packaging facility will include the production of
pre-mixed concrete with dry, fine and coarse sand for packaging and shipping and the
paving facility will include the mixing and conveying of wet aggregate to a paver/block
fabrication machine. The conveyor will be located inside and outside the two
manufacturing buildings. The materials will be poured into molds and compressed and
then cured in kilns. Once cured, the products will be placed on pallets, packaged, and
wrapped for shipping. The future manufacturing facility will be used as an expansion of
the paver manufacturing facility. The office building will be used to conduct administrative
duties of the facilities. Truck trips during normal operations are estimated at 65 trucks per
day. Approximately 45 employees will be on-site with day shift hours from 6:00 a.m. to
4:30 p.m. and swing shift hours from 4:30 p.m. to 3:00 a.m. Sunday through Saturday.

The project site is substantially surrounded by vacant land within the MRE zone.
However, there are two existing legal non-conforming residences southwest of the project
site along 75th Street East. To ensure that the facility will not be a nuisance to neighboring
properties or future development, mitigation measures and Conditions of Approval have
been applied to the project, such as the requirement to submit a dust control plan to the
AVAQMD for review and approval and the requirement that back-up and warning alarms
on all equipment be modified from an audible warning device to a visual warning device
for nighttime operations.

a)  Does the project have the potential to substantially degrade the quality of
  the environment, substantially reduce the habitat of a fish or wildlife species,
  cause a fish or wildlife population to drop below self-sustaining levels,
  threaten to eliminate a plant or animal community, substantially reduce the

  Less than Significant Impact with Mitigation Incorporated. As analyzed in the
  2022 Biological Habitat Assessment Report, the Project area was not found to
  have evidence of the presence of any state or federally listed endangered,
  threatened, rare, or sensitive species of animal. While a portion of the Project area
  is partially located within the Antelope Valley Significant Ecological Area, no rare
  species were identified on site, and no evidence was found of desert tortoise
  existing on site. The 2022 Biological Habitat Assessment Report identified the
  Project area as a suitable habitat and within the range of the Mohave ground
  squirrel, desert kit fox, and burrowing owl with recommended surveys.

  The Project area was surveyed and was found to contain approximately 79
  Western Joshua trees which would be moved or relocated as part of the Proposed
  Project. Given its status in being petitioned as a candidate threatened species, in
  addition to the potential presence of certain species on the Project area, the
  Proposed Project will implement mitigation measures MM BIO-1 through MM BIO-
  9 to reduce impacts to a less than significant level. With compliance and
  implementation of these mitigation measures, the Proposed Project will not result in
  the substantial reduction of a habitat or threaten to eliminate a natural community.

  Based on the consultation with the Fernandeño Tataviam Band of Mission Indians,

  undiscovered resources within the Project site due to its sensitivity (MM TCR-1 and
